chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who killed al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was a son of fornication, and the one who killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him) was a son of fornication.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam al-Sadiq
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنَ بْنَ عَلِيٍّ: Husayn ibn Ali, the grandson of the Prophet
key_terms.يَحْيَى بْنَ زَكَرِيَّا: Yahya ibn Zakariyya (John the son of Zechariah)

ai.seo_question: Who were the killers of Husayn ibn Ali and Yahya ibn Zakariyya in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) identifies the killer of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) and the killer of Prophet Yahya (a.s.) as 'walad zin' (sons of fornication), a title often attributed to Marwan ibn al-Hakam and Abd al-Malik respectively in Shia historiography. This comparison underscores a spiritual parallel between the Umayyad usurpers who extinguished the light of the Imams and the prophets, marking their illegitimacy not just genealogically but as archetypes of tyranny against divine authority.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 6. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Qurashi Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain (ibn Abil Khaťťāb), from Safwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Dāwūd ibn Farqad, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
The killer of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) was conceived illegitimately and the killer of Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (a.s.) was (also) conceived illegitimately.
